chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

Salim ibn Abi Hafsah and his companions were mentioned in his presence, so he said: 'They deny that those who fought against Ali (peace be upon him) were polytheists (Mushrikun).' So Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'Then they claim that they are disbelievers (Kuffar).'
Then he said to me: 'Disbelief (Kufr) precedes polytheism (Shirk).' Then he mentioned the disbelief of Iblis when He said to him, 'Prostrate,' but he refused to prostrate.

And he said: 'Disbelief precedes polytheism. So whoever is audacious against Allah, refuses obedience, and persists in major sins, he is a disbeliever (Kafir), meaning a disbeliever who is contemptuous (Mustakhiff).
ai.seo_question: What is the difference between Kufr (disbelief) and Shirk (polytheism) in Shia theology?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Baqir (AS) refutes the view of Salim ibn Abi Hafsa that those who fought Imam Ali (AS) were merely polytheists, asserting instead that their core state was disbelief (Kufr). He establishes a theological hierarchy where Kufr (denial of truth/obedience) precedes Shirk (associating partners), using Iblis’s initial refusal to prostrate as the primordial example. This distinction is crucial in Shia jurisprudence for determining whether a sinner remains within the fold of Islam or exits it entirely based on the severity of their rejection.
